summary: Exact-source audit: saved BFJ 1201.0188v1 retains function-field algebraizability and SNC support; BE 1805.01016v3 reports a descent/resolution-restricted characteristic-p envelope result. All ten source hashes verified.
detailedSummary: The original proof uses cofinal regular SNC models, skeleton equicontinuity, multiplier-ideal positivity and envelope regularization, followed by locality and algebraizability-dependent orthogonality. The saved 1201.0188 is actual v1. Its algebraizability concerns descent of X to a one-variable function field with completion K; L need not descend. BE's reported positive-characteristic envelope result instead assumes descent of (X,L) and resolution in dimension n+d. These statements do not establish the full positive-residue-characteristic finite-energy equation.
text:
The audit used only input.json, the ten listed public caches and fresh workspace artifacts.

BFJ 1201.0187v2 assumes complete discrete valuation, residue characteristic zero, smooth projective X and ample L. Its banner is 21 January 2014; its internal manuscript date is 22 October 2018. SNC cofinality enters the original psh definition and retractions. Sections 5–8 also use multiplier ideals for positivity, toroidal equicontinuity for normalized compactness, and subadditivity/global generation/vanishing for envelope regularization. Resolution alone does not replace these ideal-theoretic uses.

The actual saved 1201.0188v1 has banner 30 December 2011. Theorem A requires smooth projective X over complete discretely valued K of residue characteristic zero, ample L, and positive Radon μ of mass (L^n) supported on an SNC dual complex. X must satisfy X=Y_K for smooth projective Y over a one-variable function field F whose completion is K. The statement does not require L to descend. Appendix A uses this algebraizability for orthogonality through compactification and big-line-bundle decompositions. This saved theorem cannot be treated as a later arbitrary-support theorem.

1805.01016v3 is Boucksom–Eriksson, Spaces of norms, determinant of cohomology and Fekete points in non-Archimedean geometry. Theorem 9.15 identifies relative volume with relative MA energy for continuous psh metrics on semiample Q-line bundles on geometrically reduced projective varieties over any complete valued field. Smooth X and ample L meet these hypotheses. Section 7.30 still labels unrestricted envelope continuity conjectural. Its reported discrete characteristic-p case assumes descent of (X,L) to a function field of transcendence degree d and resolution in dimension n+d, replacing multiplier ideals with test ideals. The cited GJKM paper is not supplied, so its exact stronger resolution formulation is not independently asserted here. This report gives neither a mixed-characteristic conclusion nor an unbounded equation theorem in this draft.

Pille–Schneider 2209.04879v2, Remark 4.4, distinguishes defining E1 from extending MA to E1. Section 1.2 expressly assumes equicharacteristic zero; the shorter wording “characteristic zero” in the remark does not establish a mixed-characteristic endpoint.

summary: Published partial theorem: with positive characteristic and trivial valuation, the genuine E1 operator exists in every dimension; arbitrary-support finite-energy measures have unique solutions on smooth projective varieties of dimension at most two. This does not solve the nontrivial valuation axis.
detailedSummary: Apply Boucksom–Jonsson 1801.08229v4 over algebraically closed trivially valued k of characteristic p>0, smooth connected projective X and ample L. The canonical trivial reference has raw mass V=(L^n). The exact measure condition is sup_H{V E(u)−∫u dμ}<∞ and μ(Xan)=V. The finite-energy pairing defines an approximation-independent genuine MA measure. Comparison and injectivity hold in every dimension. Unconditional positive-characteristic surjectivity uses envelopes proved for dim X≤2, resolving test configurations of dimension n+1≤3 and replacing multiplier ideals with test ideals. Higher-dimensional surjectivity remains conditional on the envelope property.
text:
This is an application of the published theorem in Boucksom–Jonsson 1801.08229v4, not a new solution of P16.3.

Hypotheses: k is algebraically closed of characteristic p>0 with trivial absolute value; X/k is smooth, connected and projective, dimension n≥1; L is ample. Fix the canonical trivial reference metric ρ, write ω=c1(L) and V=(L^n)>0. PSH(L) consists of nontrivial usc decreasing limits of Fubini–Study functions m^{-1}max_i(log|s_i|+λ_i), using basepoint-free sections of mL and rational λ_i. Weak convergence means convergence at divisorial valuations. E(u)=(ω,u)^{n+1}/((n+1)V), extended monotonically, and E1={E>−∞}. Raw energy is V E.

The exact measure condition is positivity, μ(Xan)=V, and E*raw_ρ(μ)=sup_H[V E(u)−∫u dμ]<∞. For ν=μ/V this equals V E∨(ν), and the supremum equals that over E1. To prove this passage, take u_j∈H decreasing to u∈E1. Then E(u_j)→E(u), while ∫u_j dν≥E(u_j)−E∨(ν). Monotone integration of usc functions on compact Xan gives convergence of the integrals; their uniform lower bound proves u∈L1(ν). Every E1 expression is therefore a limit of model expressions. The reverse supremum inequality follows from H⊂E1. Constant tests give c(V−μ(Xan)); rational constants already force exact mass V whenever raw dual energy is finite. No restricted measure is renormalized.

Construction: use the finite-energy multilinear pairing of Theorem 7.14, whose existence and monotone continuity are published inputs. On PL tests define T_u(f)=(0,f)·(ω,u)^n. Theorem 7.18 gives positivity, T_u(1)=V and |T_u(f)|≤V||f||∞. PL density in C0 and Riesz representation give a unique positive Radon measure MAraw_ρ(u). Pairing continuity gives convergence against every PL test for any decreasing model approximation; the uniform bound extends convergence to all continuous tests. Thus the limit is approximation-independent. Proposition 7.19 identifies the model case with Σ_F b_F((ω_𝓧+D)|_F)^n δ_{v_F}, proves raw mass V and finite-energy integrability. Theorem A supplies strong continuity and dense image in finite-energy measures in every dimension.

Locality is Theorem 7.40 on {u>v}. Apply it to max(u,v−ε), using positivity and mass V, to obtain ∫_{u<v−ε}MAraw(v)≤∫_{u≤v−ε}MAraw(u). Infinite loci are null by finite-energy integrability. Let ε decrease to zero to obtain comparison: ∫_{u<v}MAraw(v)≤∫_{u<v}MAraw(u). Equal MA measures give I(u,v)=0. Corollary 10.4 uses divisorial energy estimates and divisorial determination to infer that u−v is locally constant; connectedness gives one constant. Injectivity holds in every dimension.

For n≤2, Theorem 5.20 proves the envelope property in characteristic p. The proof reduces obstacles to PL functions, represents envelopes by normalized base ideals, resolves a test configuration of dimension n+1≤3, then uses test ideals for subadditivity/global generation. The resulting estimate forces uniform convergence of nef approximants. Resolution and test-ideal results are background used by the published theorem, not new unrestricted claims. Actual PDF page 62 distinguishes dim X≤2 from dim 𝓧≤3; page 63 states the test-ideal replacement.

The envelope property gives normalized weak compactness by Theorem 5.11. For finite-energy ν, take a maximizing sequence for Fν(u)=E(u)−∫u dν, normalized to sup u=0. Lemma 9.15 and Corollary 9.16 bound J(u)=sup u−E(u). Compactness gives a subnet limit; upper semicontinuity of energy puts that limit u in E1. Proposition 9.19 supplies L1(ν) convergence. Consequently Fν(u)≥limsup Fν(u_j)=E∨(ν), so u actually attains the supremum.

Theorem 8.5 gives E↓(u+tf)=E(u)+t∫f MA(u)+O(t²) for PL f, uniformly in u. With the envelope property E↓ is envelope energy. For maximizing functions with defect δ_j→0 this gives t∫f MA(u_j)≤t∫f dν+δ_j+C_f t². First let j tend to the limit, then t decrease to zero, and repeat with −f. The constant maximizing sequence u_j=u proves MA(u)=ν; multiplying by V proves MAraw(u)=μ. This is the applicable variational argument of Theorem 12.8 and the positive-characteristic conclusion of Theorem 12.9.

Therefore every arbitrary-support positive Radon measure of raw mass V and finite raw dual energy has a unique finite-energy solution on these smooth projective curves and surfaces. Continuity of the solution is not asserted. For n≥3, operator construction, comparison and injectivity remain established, but surjectivity is conditional on the envelope property. This endpoint does not apply to arbitrary varieties over F_p((t)) or Q_p.

The full cited argument is in P16.3-argument.md, Section 3, and standalone P16.3-paper.tex. Literal proofs and actual PDF checks are retained in source-extracts/source-provenance.json. Rerun generation/build: python3 build_and_check.py.

summary: Full P16.3 remains unproved here. Arbitrary-field continuous/test MA and synthetic measure approximation do not construct the unbounded operator or an actual solution potential. Requested artifacts are saved; both final TeX passes succeeded.
detailedSummary: BE supplies continuous genuine MA, and BJ 2307.01697v1 supplies test orthogonality and strong approximation of finite-energy measures without a residue-characteristic restriction. The latter explicitly does not investigate finite-energy potentials; its completed measure space is not identified with E1/R. Six obligations remain on the nontrivial positive-residue-characteristic axis: singular psh compactness, envelope/model positivity replacements, genuine unbounded mixed MA, exact energy/differentiation passages, actual arbitrary-support solutions, and unbounded comparison/injectivity. The 12-page paper, provenance and exact status schema were produced. Compilation and hashes are execution evidence only.
text:
Retain complete nontrivially discretely valued K, smooth connected projective X/K in arbitrary dimension and ample L, with V=(L^n). P16.3 includes equal characteristic (p,p) and mixed characteristic (0,p). The full result is not proved.

Established background: choose a continuous semipositive model reference ρ. Genuine model MA has raw mass V. BE Propositions 8.3/8.5 and Theorems 8.4/8.18 provide continuous measures and model calculus. Ample L is semiample, and its continuous psh metrics are psh-regularizable by Theorem 7.14, meeting Theorem 8.4's hypothesis.

For PL/model tests D_θ, θ=c1(L,ρ), set Eθ(u)=((n+1)V)^{-1}Σ_j∫u(θ+dd^cu)^j∧θ^{n−j} and Jθ(ν)=sup_Dθ(Eθ(u)−∫u dν). The exact established test-side raw condition is μ(Xan)=V and VJθ(μ/V)<∞. BJ-synth 2307.01697v1 verifies projective Berkovich synthetic data using intersection measures, integration by parts and the local Hodge index theorem. Section 1.3.2 does not assert HBC=N1 over every field; its positive cone is the preimage of the ample cone, which suffices here.

Example 2.20 derives test orthogonality from BE and published relative-volume differentiation. Definition 2.15 concerns a directed limit ∫(f−u)MAθ(u)→0 for tests u<f; it does not assert continuity of a psh envelope. Theorem 2.23 proves that maximizing test sequences have MAθ(u_j) converging strongly to ν. Theorem A completes the finite-energy measure space. The introduction expressly does not investigate potentials of finite energy. These results therefore do not produce a limiting usc psh potential or identify completed measures with E1/R. The corresponding equivalence in BJ-triv cannot be imported without its missing analytic inputs.

A narrow genuine nontrivial example works in every dimension: if a smooth projective K°-model has irreducible special fiber and relatively ample extension of L, its reference satisfies MAraw(0)=Vδξ. Energy concavity and the derivative at zero give Eθ(u)≤∫u dδξ, hence Jθ(δξ)=0. This solves one reference target, not arbitrary finite-energy measures or the unbounded operator problem.

Gubler–Rabinoff 2506.13548v2 concerns classically psh functions and maximum principles and excludes MA construction from its subject. CLD 1204.6277v2 supplies characteristic-independent local forms/currents and Bedford–Taylor theory without resolution. No identification of all target global finite-energy metrics with its regularizable local class is proved here. Thuillier treats curves; Berkovich 1993 supplies analytic/étale foundations. None is substituted for higher-dimensional global equation theory.

Concrete remaining obligations:
1. Construct the intended singular psh cone with monotone approximation and normalized compactness, replacing SNC/retraction/toroidal inputs.
2. Prove model positivity and envelope regularity or an adequate variational substitute without unproved resolution or extra function-field descent, treating mixed characteristic separately.
3. Construct approximation-independent genuine mixed MA on unbounded E1, with positivity, integrability and full raw mass V.
4. Prove equality of test and E1 dual suprema and obstacle-energy differentiation on that actual space.
5. Realize every correctly massed finite-dual-energy Radon measure of arbitrary support by an actual psh potential.
6. Establish unbounded locality/comparison and injectivity modulo constants.

Alterations, base change, normalization and universal homeomorphisms are not assumed to preserve these structures. Measure density is not substituted for existence, and no restricted measure is renormalized.
